issues.legal_issue: A state legislature may enact agrarian-reform legislation that regulates rights in agricultural land and the relationship between landholders and tenants.
material_facts: The challenged measure fixed limits on landholdings and provided for tenants in possession to purchase land, subject to provisions for landholders who required land for personal cultivation.
The measure was intended to distribute ownership and control of agricultural land and prevent its concentration.
issues.conclusion: The legislation fell within the state legislative field concerning land, including land tenures, landlord-tenant relations, and the transfer of agricultural land.
issues.legal_principle: Legislative entries in the constitutional lists are not to be construed narrowly or pedantically; they receive a large and liberal interpretation that includes ancillary or subsidiary matters fairly comprehended by their terms. The Court relied on British Coal Corporation v. The King, United Provinces v. Atiqa Begum, Navinchandra Mafatlal v. The Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay City, and Thakur Amar Singhji v. State of Rajasthan.

predicates.constitutional_validity_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of legislation.
predicates.regulates_land_relations: The challenged measure regulates relations between agricultural landholders and cultivators.
predicates.concerns_agricultural_land_transfer: The challenged measure provides for the transfer or distribution of interests in agricultural land.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity proceeding concerns a measure regulating land relations and agricultural land transfers, the rule identifies the state legislature as competent to enact it.

issues.legal_issue: Interests in land held under an existing land-tenure system that recognizes occupancy rights are estates for the purpose of constitutional protection of laws modifying rights in estates.
material_facts: The landholders held interests in agricultural land, including land under the cultivation of tenants.
The existing land-tenure law treated occupancy as a tenure and recognized occupancy as heritable and transferable.
The governing definition of estate covered interests in land, and the landholder definition did not distinguish between alienated and unalienated land.
issues.conclusion: The landholders’ interests, including interests in unalienated land, fell within the meaning of an estate for the constitutional protection at issue.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(2)(a) takes the meaning of estate from the existing law relating to land tenures in the area. The Court read the land-tenure definition of estate to encompass any interest in land and relied on the provisions recognizing occupants’ status and heritable and transferable occupancy rights. It also referred to Baia Sri Sailendra Narayan Bhanja Deo v. State of Orissa; it distinguished the interpretive context of Hariprasad Shivshankar Shukla v. A.D. Divikar and discussed Re The Vexatious Actions Act, 1896, In re Bernard Boaler.

predicates.constitutional_validity_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of legislation.
predicates.holding_is_an_interest_in_land: A landholder holds an interest in land under the applicable land-tenure system.
predicates.tenure_system_recognizes_occupancy_right: The existing land-tenure system recognizes occupancy as a tenure and treats occupancy rights as heritable or transferable.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity proceeding concerns a landholding that is an interest in land under a tenure system recognizing occupancy rights, the rule treats that holding as an estate for constitutional protection.

issues.legal_issue: A law that transfers title in an estate to a tenant on a specified trigger, subject only to specified events that can defeat the transfer, modifies or extinguishes the landholder’s rights and is protected from challenges based on specified fundamental rights.
material_facts: The measure provided that tenants would be deemed to have purchased qualifying land on a specified day.
The tenant’s title passed on that day and remained effective unless the tenant declined to purchase or failed to pay the purchase price as required.
The provisions therefore transferred title rather than merely suspending the landholder’s title.
issues.conclusion: The measure provided for extinguishment or modification of rights in estates and was protected from challenge under Articles 14, 19, and 31; the asserted fundamental-rights challenges could not succeed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1)(a) separately covers acquisition by the State and extinguishment or modification of rights in an estate; extinguishment or modification need not occur in the course of State acquisition. The Court held that title passed on the statutory trigger and was defeasible only on specified events. It distinguished Thakur Raghubir Singh v. Court of Wards, Ajmer, which concerned suspension of a right of management rather than transfer of title.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_proceeding and holding_is_an_estate and transfer_to_tenant_occurs_at_trigger and title_passes_immediately and title_is_defeasible_only_on_specified_events

predicates.constitutional_validity_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of legislation.
predicates.holding_is_an_estate: The affected landholding is an estate for the purpose of constitutional protection.
predicates.transfer_to_tenant_occurs_at_trigger: The law provides for the tenant to acquire the land on a specified legal trigger.
predicates.title_passes_immediately: The landholder’s title passes to the tenant when the legal trigger occurs.
predicates.title_is_defeasible_only_on_specified_ev: The transferred title can be defeated only if specified events, such as the tenant declining the purchase or defaulting on payment, occur.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity proceeding concerns an estate whose title transfers to a tenant at a trigger and is defeasible only on specified events, the rule treats the law as protected from the asserted fundamental-rights challenge.

issues.legal_issue: Delegating authority to adjust legislative limits is not excessive when the legislature has settled the policy and broad principles and the delegated discretion is bounded by relevant criteria.
material_facts: The legislature itself set the ordinary limits for landholdings and economic holdings and stated the agrarian-reform policy.

The delegated authority could vary those limits only on a public-interest basis, having regard to the land’s situation, productive capacity, location in a backward area, and other prescribed factors of the same kind.
The measure did not authorize variation for an individual’s private benefit or on an unrelated consideration.
issues.conclusion: The delegation was not excessive, and the provision authorizing variations was valid.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature may leave matters of detail to the executive after settling policy and broad principles. The Court relied on State of Bihar v. Maharajadhiraja Sir Kameshwar Singh of Darbhanga, Dr. N.B. Khare v. State of Delhi, State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar, and Pannalal Binjraj v. Union of India. It also applied the principle that a law is not invalid merely because delegated discretion might be abused; the abuse, if established, may be challenged separately.

predicates.constitutional_validity_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of legislation.
predicates.legislature_sets_policy_and_broad_princi: The legislature states the policy and broad principles governing the delegated authority.
predicates.delegation_is_limited_by_relevant_criter: The delegated authority must act with regard to criteria connected to the subject and in the public interest.
predicates.residual_criteria_are_similar_in_kind: Any additional criteria are limited to factors similar in kind to the criteria expressly stated.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity proceeding concerns a delegation bounded by legislative policy and relevant, related criteria, the rule treats the delegation as not excessive.

issues.legal_issue: A measure enacted within the legislature’s authority as a genuine agrarian reform is not colourable legislation merely because it transfers land to tenants.
material_facts: The measure regulated agricultural land, imposed holding limits, and provided for transfer of excess land to tenants in possession.
Tenants were required to pay a price fixed through the statutory process, and a purchase could become ineffective on specified payment defaults.
The legislation pursued agrarian reform and was not an attempt to use one legislative subject as a guise to exercise power outside the legislature’s authority.
issues.conclusion: The measure was not colourable legislation.
issues.legal_principle: Once the legislation was found to fall within the state legislative field concerning land, the Court found no basis for a claim that the legislature had used that field as a guise to do something beyond its competence. The Court also considered the reform’s operation, including the tenant’s obligation to pay the determined price and the consequences of default.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_proceeding and measure_is_within_legislative_field and measure_pursues_genuine_land_reform and purchaser_must_pay_for_transfer

predicates.constitutional_validity_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding challenging the constitutional validity of legislation.
predicates.measure_is_within_legislative_field: The challenged measure concerns a subject within the enacting legislature’s authority.
predicates.measure_pursues_genuine_land_reform: The challenged measure seeks to reform landholding and distribute agricultural land rather than conceal an exercise of authority outside the legislature’s field.
predicates.purchaser_must_pay_for_transfer: The measure requires the acquiring tenant to pay a price determined through the statutory process.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity proceeding concerns a measure within the legislature’s field that pursues genuine land reform and requires payment for the transfer, the rule treats the measure as not colourable.
